text.name: vtsz_help_cropReq_intro_static
text.text: This list is built from the loaded map when you open the help.

text.name: vtsz_help_cropReq_intro
text.text: Each crop shows what one average harvest removes from the soil, in kg/ha: N, P2O5, K2O. The first line is a grain harvest with the straw chopped, so it stays on the field. Baling the straw or a forage harvest removes it too; those totals are listed where they differ. The maps show the distance from the soil type target, so no target values are listed here. Base-game FERTILIZER adds only N unless baseFertilizer is enabled in the config.

text.name: vtsz_help_om
text.text: The soil loses organic matter (OM) every month. Silage, forage-harvester or mower cuts (crop and straw leave the field) and root crops take more. Compensate with manure, chopped straw, ploughed-in catch crops or a grass / alfalfa break. Fertilizer does not raise OM. OM changes %sx faster than in reality, so one real year is about six game years.

text.name: vtsz_help_cropReq_baled
text.text: Baled straw: N %s | P2O5 %d | K2O %d kg/ha

text.name: vtsz_help_cropReq_forage
text.text: Forage harvest: N %s | P2O5 %d | K2O %d kg/ha

text.name: vtsz_help_fert_intro
text.text: Each product shows its content per 1000 litres: N, P2O5, K2O in kg. What you put on the field is the rate in l/ha times this value divided by 1000. OM is the organic matter gain in percentage points per 1000 l/ha (the OM map changes %sx faster than in reality). Lime shows the pH rise per 1000 l/ha. Base-game FERTILIZER adds only N unless baseFertilizer is enabled in the config.

text.name: vtsz_function_bag
text.text: Big bag of fertilizer for spreaders.

text.name: vtsz_function_ibc
text.text: 1000 l IBC of liquid fertilizer for sprayers.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_order
text.text: 1. Take soil samples and check the pH. On acid soil phosphorus works badly: lime first (lime or Carbolime). 2. P and K base dressing before sowing, worked in. 3. Organic manure on the stubble or before ploughing. 4. N top dressing in spring, split into two doses. 5. Replace what the harvest removed. After the harvest the field info box shows the gap, and the automatic rate fills exactly up to the target.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_rates
text.text: The l/ha bands on this page are typical practice, converted to game litres with the product densities. They are not taken from a source. The exact dose is the gap in the field info box. Where the text says realistic or in reality, it is advice: the mod does not model it. What the mod really does is under Game rules.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_nitrogen
text.text: CAN 27: the standard spring top dressing for cereals, rapeseed and grass. About 150-250 l/ha per pass. Urea: cheap N for maize, sunflower and cereals. In reality it loses ammonia from the surface in warm dry weather, so work it in or spread it before rain. About 135-265 l/ha. Nitrosol UAN: liquid, exact, easy to split. Sprayer in spring on cereals and rapeseed, between maize rows. About 100-200 l/ha.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_phosphorus
text.text: Phosphorus hardly moves in the soil, so in reality it is worked in before sowing. MAP (11-52-0): starter P for cold spring soil, before sowing or at sowing, for maize, beet, sunflower and rapeseed. About 50-210 l/ha, starter rates at the low end. Triple superphosphate: pure P base dressing, in autumn before ploughing or before sowing, for every crop. About 90-180 l/ha. Single superphosphate (0-18-0): weak, but it contains sulphur (not modelled), which rapeseed and legumes need. Autumn before sowing. About 190-380 l/ha: a lot of material.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_potassium
text.text: Potassium chloride 60 (MOP): the cheapest K. Autumn or early spring, also onto the growing crop. About 90-230 l/ha, for beet and silage maize up to about 270. In reality the chloride harms potatoes and vegetables: keep it off them, or spread it long before sowing in autumn (the mod does not model this). At most 450 l/ha per pass. Patentkali (0-0-30): chloride-free K with magnesium and sulphur (not modelled). Expensive, so keep it for potatoes, vegetables, beet and rapeseed. About 170-340 l/ha.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_npk
text.text: NPK 15-15-15: even all-round fertilizer for the spring seedbed or as top dressing, if you did not calculate and the gap is small. Maize, sunflower, spring top-up of cereals. About 190-285 l/ha. NPK 8-24-24: the classic autumn base for winter wheat, winter barley and rapeseed. Little N, which is all autumn needs, and much P and K. About 190-285 l/ha.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_organic
text.text: Manure: the main humus source. In autumn on the stubble, worked in at once, before maize, beet and silage maize. Example: 20000 l/ha = +140 N, +35 P2O5, +84 K2O. Slurry: early spring before sowing, or autumn on the stubble. Much N and K, little P and humus. Example: 25000 l/ha = +100 N, +42 P2O5, +125 K2O. Digestate: like slurry, fast N, little humus. Yeast vinasse: cheap K, little N, a little organic matter. About 1600-2500 l/ha (the automatic rate stops at 2500). The N of organic fertilizer limits the dose: too much N lowers the yield.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_lime
text.text: Carbolime (sugar factory lime sludge) raises the pH, so phosphorus works better. Use it in autumn on the stubble of acid fields. Typical practice is 5-10 t/ha, depending on the pH. In the game it also gives 18 kg P2O5 and 1.2 kg K2O per 1000 l. Not every map has it.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_calA
text.text: July-August (after harvest): manure, slurry, vinasse and Carbolime on the stubble. P and K base dressing for the winter crops (NPK 8-24-24, TSP, MOP). September-October: NPK 8-24-24 or MAP into the seedbed of wheat, barley and rapeseed. P, K and manure onto the fields of the spring crops, before ploughing. November: MOP and P/K base dressing before ploughing, if the soil is not frozen. In standing winter crops at most MOP, no N. December to mid-February: nothing (see the house rules).

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_calB
text.text: Late February-March: first N top dressing on the winter crops (CAN, Nitrosol). NPK 15-15-15 if the autumn base dressing was skipped. March-April: slurry, digestate, urea worked in. MAP starter under maize, beet and sunflower. Second N dose on the winter crops. May-June: Nitrosol between the maize rows. Slurry after cutting grass. Late N on heading cereals brings little.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_cropCereal
text.text: Winter wheat (removal 64 / 44 P2O5 / K2O, with baled straw +19 / +90): NPK 8-24-24 in the October seedbed. CAN or Nitrosol in late February and April. Winter barley (56 / 42, straw +15 / +120): NPK 8-24-24 in September. CAN in early spring, one or two doses. Rapeseed (55 / 30): NPK 8-24-24, or SSP + MOP, in late August before sowing. CAN or Nitrosol in February and March.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_cropMaize
text.text: Grain maize (62 / 55): in autumn before ploughing manure, or TSP + MOP. MAP as starter at sowing. Urea worked in, or Nitrosol between the rows. Silage maize (65 / 190): manure in autumn, slurry in spring, with MOP. Nitrosol between the rows. Potassium is the main removal. Sunflower (56 / 84): in autumn TSP + MOP, in spring NPK 15-15-15. Little N.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_cropBeet
text.text: Sugar beet (70 / 175): in autumn manure + MOP (and Carbolime on acid soil), in spring MAP. N before sowing, not later (sugar content). Potato (56 / 240): in autumn manure, in spring Patentkali (chloride-free). CAN at ridging. Silage maize, beet and potato remove the most K, so replacing K matters most there.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_cropLegume
text.text: Alfalfa (20 / 93 per cut): plenty of SSP + MOP before sowing. No N, it is a legume. K every year for the hay removal. Grass (22 / 87 per cut): MOP in early spring, slurry after the cuts.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_rulesA
text.text: Product lock: the same product counts once per pixel, until tillage, sowing or harvest releases it. Spread the full amount in one pass. Two different products both count on the P, K and OM map. N cap: a P or K based automatic rate never applies more N than Precision Farming would. With an N-rich product (MAP, NPK, vinasse, manures) a P or K gap often cannot be filled: use TSP, SSP, MOP or Patentkali. Two N products in a row: the N of the second one does not reach the Precision Farming nitrogen map without tillage in between (known limitation).

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_rulesB
text.text: MOP: at most 450 l/ha per pass (about 297 kg K2O). For a bigger gap add Patentkali, or pass again after tillage, sowing or harvest. Phosphorus: soft cap of +300 kg/ha above the target. Whatever goes above is lost. Potassium above the target leaches slowly, more on light soils and in wet, cool months. From about +200 a mild yield penalty starts (0.97 at +400). Building up K is a loss. Baled straw takes 90 (wheat) or 120 (barley) kg K2O/ha. Chopped straw leaves it on the field.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_rulesC
text.text: Yield: of P and K the lower factor counts (law of the minimum). Organic matter multiplies on top of that. Automatic rate: Left Alt + , for products without N, otherwise the Precision Farming button. It works only on soil-sampled pixels, elsewhere the manual rate (Left Alt + K / M) applies. The automatic rate fills exactly up to the target, every year. After a harvest the field info box shows the new gap.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_houseA
text.text: The mod does not punish bad timing, so keep realism with server rules. These are suggestions, not mod behaviour. P only before sowing or tillage, not into the standing crop (surface P works slowly in reality). No spreading from December 1 to February 15 (general guidance from memory: check the local nitrate regulation). Work manure in on the same game day.

text.name: vtsz_help_guide_houseB
text.text: Organic N: the EU nitrates directive limit is 170 kg N/ha and year from livestock manure (from memory: check local regulation). That is about 42000 l/ha slurry or 24000 l/ha manure. Potato and vegetables: Patentkali, or MOP already in the previous autumn. Urea only worked in or before rain. If you do not want the automatic rate to fill perfectly every year: spread at most 1.5 times the removal per year and build deficits up over several years.
